segments: Chronography of Barhebraeus.
36 ... to Babylon.
And he subdued Europus, Hyrcania, and Mauria.
And he took all of Asia Major;
he also crossed the Indus River,
and he subdued India and took captives.
And he took to wife Roxana, daughter of Darius,
and also took her sister captive with her.
And he built twelve cities.
And he made an iron gate,
so that the Huns might not go out;
its length was twelve cubits, and its breadth eight.
And he took the Jews,
and they received him,
and he sacrificed to God.
And when the Samaritans killed Andromachus, the governor {or: priest} whom he had left with them,
he came from Egypt and destroyed them,
and settled Macedonians in Samaria.
And when he came to Babylon,
after he had reigned twelve years and seven months,
one of his nobles killed him with poison.
And the great horn was broken,
and four horns arose from under it,
that is to say, his servants who reigned after him.
The years from Adam until the death of Alexander add up,
according to Annianus the monk, to 5069;
five thousand and sixty-nine.
And in the time of Alexander lived Andromachus the physician, who added viper's flesh to the antidote mithridate,
and it was beneficial against the bites of vipers.
Ptolemy {OCR?}, his servant, [reigned] forty years;
and he is the son of Lagus, that is,
the son of the hare.
He arose after him in Alexandria,
and brought his body and buried him there.
And in the year he became king, he took Jerusalem by deceit,
and took a captivity of Jews,
and settled them in Egypt in the days of Onias the high priest.
And from him onward the kings were known as the Ptolemies.
Over the Macedonians, however, reigned Philip Arrhidaeus.
And in Syria reigned Antiochus,
and Seleucus Nicator became his partner in the kingdom,
that is,
the Victorious.
In Cilicia, however, and in Asia, and in Caria, and in the Hellespont, and in Thrace, and in Paphlagonia, and in Epirus—
in other manuscripts: and in Europe—
seven other kings arose,
so that in all they were ten.
And the word of Daniel was fulfilled,
that the beast had ten horns {OCR?}.
